newsitem.title: USA: US attache sees Russia boosting cotton imports.
newsitem.headline: US attache sees Russia boosting cotton imports.

text.p: Russia could import 230,000 tonnes of cotton in 1997/8 (August-July), up from an estimated 210,000 tonnes in the current marketing year, the USDA attache in Moscow said.
In a May 20 report released today, the attache noted that Russia cotton consumption has stabilized at about 240,000 to 250,000 tonnes annually, down about 50 percent from the late 1980s.

U.S cotton shipments to Russia are expected to reach 15,000 tonnes in 1996/7, the said. But limited demand for high-quality fabrics made in Russia could restrict growth in cotton imports from the United States the attache said.

Still, the removal of a value-added tax on cotton from outside most countries of the former Soviet Union has helped the United States compete against supplies from Central Asia, particularly Uzbekistan, the attache said.
Uzbekistan supplies about 70 percent of Russia's cotton imports.
